scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.

Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. scenarios.oracle: the value carries its unit at the boundary (pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent) - the class that made a knob of 10 mean 1000%

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.

findings.title: banked green for a non-HTTP layer on evidence taken only at the PostgREST gateway - the edge envelope is demonstrably a different shape
findings.detail: I banked envelope_shape and status_body_agreement for EVERY layer subject on one measurement: real GETs against http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1. That measurement is sound for the client/gateway/db layers and says NOTHING about this row's layer. The proof that it is a different question, taken minutes later once the edge runtime was restarted: POST {} to /functions/v1/ai-gateway answers 400 with the body {"error":"Missing agent"} - ONE key. The PostgREST envelope this row was banked on is {code, message, details, hint} - FOUR keys, and the row's own evidence asserts all four are present. So the edge layer does not satisfy the property this row was marked green for, and if it had been probed the verdict might well have been a finding. HOW IT HAPPENED: the banker iterated every CA layer row on the page and applied the same gateway result to all of them, using R7/page_layer_deps to get the DEPENDENCIES right while never checking that the MEASUREMENT matched the layer. Correct anchoring on the wrong evidence still yields a false green - an oracle that does not match its claim. AND THE EDGE RUNTIME WAS DOWN THE WHOLE TIME: supabase_edge_runtime_workhive had been 'Exited (255) 4 days ago', so at the moment of banking every edge function on the platform was answering 503. A layer claim banked while that layer is not running cannot be anything but false, and nothing in the banker noticed - the reading came from a different service that WAS up. `docker start` brought it back and it now serves 58 functions. TO RE-EARN: probe the layer this row actually names. For edge/ai/external-send that is /functions/v1/<fn> with apikey + a member JWT (tools/backend_edge_probe.py has the helpers; note its anon_key() returns '' on this stack because it only accepts legacy eyJ JWTs - prove_http_envelope.resolve_key() carries the working fallback). For cron/realtime/print/cdn the envelope question needs its own instrument and the row should stay owed until one exists, rather than inheriting a reading from whatever service happened to answer.

withdrawn_evidence.asserts: none of this page's read relations is reachable through the probed gateway surface, so there is no envelope here to check - recorded as vacuous rather than counted as proof
withdrawn_evidence.checked: DECLARED-NA ON A MEASURED DENOMINATOR (rail R10). This page's 3 read relation(s) do not intersect the 40 probed at the gateway. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself.

findings.title: QUALIFIED - invalid-but-present enum returns 200 (analytics-orchestrator accepts any phase)
findings.detail: QUALIFIED BY A LATER MEASUREMENT IN THE SAME SESSION - flagged rather than left standing. This row was banked on four edge probes: 400 naming a missing field, 400 from a second function naming a different missing field, 404 for an unknown function, and 200 for a successful run. That evidence holds. But it did NOT include an INVALID-BUT-PRESENT field value, and probing that afterwards found analytics-orchestrator returns 200 for ANY phase string - metrics, analyze, summary, phase1 all returned 200 with the invalid phase ECHOED BACK, plus period_days:90 and a generated_at, even though the function's own source recognises only report, descriptive, diagnostic, predictive and prescriptive. So `phase` is validated for PRESENCE and never for VALIDITY. WHY THAT BEARS ON THIS ORACLE: a 200 returning a result for an input the function does not recognise is a response whose status claims success for a request that was not actually understood. My banked wording said 'no 200-carrying-an-error', which was true of the cases I probed and is not established for this one. I am recording the qualification rather than quietly leaving the green, because a row that a later measurement undercuts is exactly the drift this bank exists to prevent - and because the same session that earned the row found the counter-case. NOT WITHDRAWN, and the reasoning is stated so it can be overruled: the four probed cases genuinely agree, and the new case is better classified as an input-VALIDATION defect than a status/body disagreement - the body IS internally consistent with the 200 it carries. Whether an unvalidated enum should return 400 is a design call on the function, not a contradiction between its status and its body. If the next walk judges otherwise, withdraw this row with a false-green-withdrawn finding; the evidence for both readings is recorded here. TO FINISH: validate `phase` against the known set in analytics-orchestrator and return 400 naming the valid values (the function already returns 400 with a named field for absence, so the pattern exists); then re-probe the invalid-enum case and settle this row without a qualification. Per A15 no edit was made - the edit budget is closed and it belongs in the next batched wave.
findings.observed: phase=metrics|analyze|summary|phase1 all -> 200 with the phase echoed; source recognises only report|descriptive|diagnostic|predictive|prescriptive

findings.title: banked green for a non-HTTP layer on evidence taken only at the PostgREST gateway - the edge envelope is demonstrably a different shape
findings.detail: I banked envelope_shape and status_body_agreement for EVERY layer subject on one measurement: real GETs against http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1. That measurement is sound for the client/gateway/db layers and says NOTHING about this row's layer. The proof that it is a different question, taken minutes later once the edge runtime was restarted: POST {} to /functions/v1/ai-gateway answers 400 with the body {"error":"Missing agent"} - ONE key. The PostgREST envelope this row was banked on is {code, message, details, hint} - FOUR keys, and the row's own evidence asserts all four are present. So the edge layer does not satisfy the property this row was marked green for, and if it had been probed the verdict might well have been a finding. HOW IT HAPPENED: the banker iterated every CA layer row on the page and applied the same gateway result to all of them, using R7/page_layer_deps to get the DEPENDENCIES right while never checking that the MEASUREMENT matched the layer. Correct anchoring on the wrong evidence still yields a false green - an oracle that does not match its claim. AND THE EDGE RUNTIME WAS DOWN THE WHOLE TIME: supabase_edge_runtime_workhive had been 'Exited (255) 4 days ago', so at the moment of banking every edge function on the platform was answering 503. A layer claim banked while that layer is not running cannot be anything but false, and nothing in the banker noticed - the reading came from a different service that WAS up. `docker start` brought it back and it now serves 58 functions. TO RE-EARN: probe the layer this row actually names. For edge/ai/external-send that is /functions/v1/<fn> with apikey + a member JWT (tools/backend_edge_probe.py has the helpers; note its anon_key() returns '' on this stack because it only accepts legacy eyJ JWTs - prove_http_envelope.resolve_key() carries the working fallback). For cron/realtime/print/cdn the envelope question needs its own instrument and the row should stay owed until one exists, rather than inheriting a reading from whatever service happened to answer.

withdrawn_evidence.asserts: none of this page's read relations is reachable through the probed gateway surface, so there is no envelope here to check - recorded as vacuous rather than counted as proof
withdrawn_evidence.checked: DECLARED-NA ON A MEASURED DENOMINATOR (rail R10). This page's 3 read relation(s) do not intersect the 40 probed at the gateway. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - fail_401: an expired session is not surfaced honestly on this page. THIS FAILS ON 17 OF 17 PAGES WALKED, and the fix is ADOPTION, not a new message
findings.detail: FAILURE STATES ARE INJECTED, never waited for. failures() intercepts the page's own reads and answers them with the failure under test, then reads what the page TELLS A PERSON. Every mutating verb is answered by a stub rather than forwarded - decided by blockWrite across the WHOLE Supabase surface, rpc and edge functions included - so nothing reaches the shared test database. The path is verified unchanged across the injection, and the surface is asserted before it: an expired session earlier today made 19 of 22 pages return identical landing-page readings, and 3 pages were REFUSED by that guard on this very sweep rather than measured. The navigation fence held on 16 of 16 pages read. THE ORACLE IS WHAT THE READER IS TOLD, not whether an error was caught. A caught error that renders nothing is indistinguishable, from the reader's side, from success. Stamped ::v=3: the top-level digest is a SET of per-statement content hashes, so a shared-library append expires nothing while a modify or delete correctly expires. Self-tested 8/8. FINDING: Injecting a 401 into this page's reads, the page does not tell the reader their session expired, does not name the session as the cause, and does not state the consequence for what they were doing. THE REFLEX IS TO WRITE THE MISSING MESSAGE AND THAT WOULD BE WRONG - it already exists. utils.js:1568 reads 'Your session expired, so nothing was saved. Sign in again and redo this step.' and :1611 has the read equivalent, with _WH_PG_DENIAL at :1518 and a careful 401-versus-403 note beneath it. There is even a comment recording that this was fixed once on the inquiry path, where a 42501 told a SIGNED-IN buyer their session had expired, and that 'the shared helper kept the bug for every other path'. Writing a new string would add a second source of truth for text that is already correct. SO THE DEFECT IS ADOPTION: the read path catches the status and never renders whReadError's text. A uniform 17-of-17 failure is not seventeen independent lapses, it is one shared path swallowing the status - which means ONE fix earns all seventeen rows in a single sweep. Same shape as the other platform-wide finds in this arc: ::placeholder absent everywhere, companion-launcher.js with no prefers-reduced-motion block at all. AND THE PROBE IS NOT AT FAULT, which matters before acting on a 17/17 result: fail_null_field passes on 16 of 16 pages under the same injection harness. A broken probe does not pass one injection everywhere and fail another everywhere. Row stays owed; measure adoption at the point of RENDER, not by the helper's existence.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. That is a sentence describing FEATURES to a person, not an assertion about a table, and analytics is right on its own terms - it reads analytics_snapshots, a snapshot DERIVED from logbook data, which is precisely what 'saved snapshot ... based on your logbook' says. A keyword match over human prose is how a page's own helper text becomes a defect. The test now counts a token only when it is unmistakably schema-shaped (a v_ prefix, a _truth suffix, or a known table prefix + underscore); bare English words never qualify. ★AND THE VIEW IS READ INSIDE ITSELF. V1 is graded at page scope and V2 inside the OPENED view via the shared tools/dialog_targets.mjs registry, because crediting a V2 row with a V1 reading is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this bank has already paid for once. NOT BANKED GREEN: this view displays NO source chip at all (0 on screen while the surface requested 6 relation(s)). A surface that makes no provenance claim has not made a TRUE one, and the oracle asks whether the claim is true - so silence cannot satisfy it. Scoring it green would credit the absence of a promise as a kept promise. THIS IS ALSO NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT. Most of the 23 are V2 dialogs - a composer, a confirm sheet, a detail panel - which display a form rather than a derived figure, and a provenance chip on a surface that states no number would be noise. WHAT SETTLES IT is the per-view question the bank actually asks: does THIS view show a figure a reader would want provenance for? If yes, the chip is missing and this is a real finding; if no, the row is declared-na under R10 with 'this view states no derived figure' as the reason and the CM comprehension oracles as its replacement. Left owed rather than guessed, because that question is per-view and answering it from a count would be inventing the verdict.

Most numbers on this platform are COUNTS - 9 open jobs, 28 PMs overdue - and a count has no unit to show; flagging those would redden every surface, and a check that reddens everything is measuring itself. (1) It first accepted only BARE digits, so any value already carrying its unit never entered the set - 21 of 22 pages reported '0 judged' on a platform that renders MTBF and OEE nearly everywhere. An implausible abstention is an instrument fault, not a finding. (2) It then failed analytics on 'total downtime = 717.9h' because the time vocabulary listed hr/hrs/hours but not a bare 'h'. An oracle's vocabulary IS the oracle. Both are fixed and recorded in the tool. That one asks whether something adjacent NAMES the figure and the roster passes it 79/79. This asks whether a person can say what the number MEANS: 'PM compliance 61%%' is named and unexplained - 61%% of WHAT, over WHAT window, counted HOW? ★ONLY DERIVED FIGURES OWE AN EXPLANATION, and getting that wrong would redden every surface. A raw COUNT explains itself - 'Open Jobs 9' is nine jobs. A PERCENTAGE, RATE, SCORE, INDEX or COMPOSITE is computed from things the reader cannot see, and that is where the meaning lives off-screen. Any ONE of a denominator, a window, a derivation or a definition discharges the obligation; requiring all four would fail good surfaces. ★THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG THREE TIMES BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, each caught by disbelieving the output: (1) EIGHTEEN abstentions on a platform that renders OEE and MTBF - analytics' KPI heroes live behind its phase panels, not the landing view, so the prover now reaches the view that owns the metric; (2) it failed hive's 'HEALTHY /100 composite risk - lower is better', a figure that states its scale AND its direction, because my denominator pattern demanded a digit on BOTH sides of the slash; (3) it failed project-report on 'Replace mechanical seal + bearings Leandro Mar... = 4.0' because the enclosing block resolved to a whole TABLE and every cell inherited the section's derived-ness - adjacency is not several hundred characters of table, so table cells are now excluded and long labels skipped. evidence.asserts: repeating an identical write does not create a second record, and the guarantee is enforced by a constraint rather than by the client
evidence.checked: PROVEN BY REPEATING THE WRITE, inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member. The same row - same primary key, same payload - was inserted twice in one transaction. The second attempt was refused: 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint logbook_pkey'. So a repeat cannot create a second record, and the guarantee comes from a CONSTRAINT rather than from client-side de-duplication that a double-tap, a retry, or an offline queue drain could outrun. WHY THE CONSTRAINT IS THE RIGHT PLACE FOR IT: this platform queues field-capture writes offline and drains them on reconnect, so the same logical write can genuinely arrive twice from two directions. A uniqueness guarantee that lives in the page dies with the page's assumptions; one that lives in the index holds for the queue drain, the retry and the second tab alike. VERIFIED CLEAN: 0 probe rows survived. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13. SCOPE: this settles the REPEAT of an identical write. It does not settle a second write with a DIFFERENT client-generated id representing the same intent - that is the offline-queue collapse question and lives on its own seam row.
evidence.value_checked: second identical insert refused by logbook_pkey; 0 rows after rollback

Its sentence says 'Try again.' but no control exists to do so. SO THE ONLY RECOURSE IS A FULL RELOAD, which on a phone in a plant costs the whole page again on the connection that just failed. THE PATTERN EXISTS ON THIS PLATFORM, so this is adoption: achievements renders a Retry button beside its toast, and public-feed's Retry was measured firing a real re-request and then rendering 15 post cards. Only 2 of 22 pages have one. WHAT WOULD PASS IT: a control that RE-ISSUES the failed read - the probe counts requests fired after the click, so a button that merely re-renders the previous failure fails too. That is the exact defect commit 3ddef99d fixed on public-feed. MEASURED BY ANSWERING EVERY READ WITH A 500 AT window.fetch AND READING WHAT THE PAGE SAYS NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request resolves to a synthetic `{"code":"500"}` with Content-Type application/json; `/auth/v1/` is untouched so the session survives, which is what makes this a SERVER fault rather than a dead network. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. Every claim below quotes the page's own visible sentence, collected from leaf-ish elements under a composed-visibility test (getClientRects + checkVisibility + an ancestor walk for display/visibility/opacity) so hidden template copy cannot be mistaken for something a reader sees. TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS SWEEP WERE THROWN AWAY, WHICH IS WHY THE NUMBERS HERE ARE TRUSTED. The first used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered live data - a registered service worker sits between page and transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. The second omitted the identity guard and returned byte-identical output for seven different pages (14,677 chars of marketing copy) because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. This version guards INSIDE the evaluate: expected uid, `location.pathname` ends in the page's own file, and body chars outside the 13,000-16,000 landing band - refusing rather than reporting. PLATFORM RESULT, all 22 pages: **9 state the failure in domain language** (hive, inventory, dayplanner, pm-scheduler, index, skillmatrix, achievements, voice-journal, assistant) and **11 say nothing or assert a falsehood**. MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean. ★THE INDUCTION IS PROVEN TO HAVE LANDED, which is the difference between a verdict and a guess: the lens reports inductionLanded, the number of reads that actually went out under the injected condition, and refuses to score a page that never re-queried. Its own comment records why - it once read retry_path:false / fallback:silentlyStale on a surface that handles both correctly, because closure-scoped loaders meant the page never moved, and it scored the UNCHANGED page. Every verdict banked here carries inductionLanded > 0 and inconclusive:false. ★AND THE LENS IS PROVEN ABLE TO PASS, so a FAIL is not a blanket instrument failure: across the roster it returned retry_path 3 PASS / 19 FAIL, rate_limit_legible 1/21, fallback_engaged 7/15, slow_honest 10/12. public-feed passes all four - consistent with its own history, since it is the page fixed so a failed read renders an error rather than 'No public posts yet'. RETRY PATH - FAILS, and the half that is certain is the half that matters. Under an injected 500 this page offers ZERO retry affordances: no 'try again', no 'reload', no 'refresh' control. That is confirmed TWO independent ways - the lens counted affordances:0, and a separate direct probe that 500'd every /rest/v1/ request and scanned the whole document for a retry control also found none. A person whose data failed to load has nothing to press. ★ONE HALF OF THIS VERDICT IS INSTRUMENT-DEPENDENT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN BANKED AS FACT: the lens also reported saysFailure:True. My direct probe, which failed EVERY read rather than the subset the lens induces, and which scanned the whole page rather than <main>, found that this page DOES say something failed under a total outage. So the page's failure MESSAGING may be better than the lens's number suggests - a partial induction can leave a surface half-populated and quiet. The missing retry CONTROL is not in doubt; the missing failure SENTENCE is, on this page. WHY IT IS NOT BANKED GREEN ANYWAY: the oracle asks for a retry PATH, and a failure a person cannot act on is the shape this family exists to catch - 'a failure that offers a retry which does not re-attempt is worse than one that offers none', and offering none at all is the floor of that same scale.

★RETRACTED CONTEXT ON THIS ROW'S RECORDED TALLY: it lists rate_limit_legible as 1P/21F. That figure is true of THIS LENS and misleading about the platform, and is retracted as evidence of any gap. 42 rate_limit_legible rows are banked green on a 2026-08-09 induction against the REAL limit - 400 logbook inserts inside BEGIN...ROLLBACK as an authenticated member, refused with 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' plus HINT logbook_daily_user, and a second hive-tier quota at SQLSTATE 54000 that states its remedy. THE PLATFORM'S RATE LIMITING IS LEGIBLE. This lens asked a different question - whether a page's TEXT names a limit under a FAKE 429 injected at the fetch layer, a client-rendering question about a condition the server never produced. PRECEDENCE (roadmap 6l/6m): a prover that induced the REAL condition outranks a lens that simulated one; the disagreement is scope, never regression. THE VERDICT ON THIS ROW'S OWN KEY IS UNAFFECTED - it rests on its own induction, which landed (inductionLanded > 0).

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_retry_path.mjs (new) - EVERY /rest/v1/ read failed with a 500, then the network released and the retry pressed. ★THE INDUCTION IS TOTAL, NOT PARTIAL, AND THAT CHANGED THE ANSWER. The availability lens fails a SUBSET of reads and reported 'affordances: 0' for pages that demonstrably DO render a Retry on other paths. Failing every request is what actually reaches a page's error branch. ★AND BOTH CLAUSES ARE MEASURED, because the second is the one that ships broken: a retry must RE-ATTEMPT and the failure must CLEAR. hive proved why - its first fix sent 3 fresh reads and left the page byte-for-byte unchanged, because it re-rendered from a cache still holding the failed state. Six pages passing is what separates 'nobody built this' from 'not every read path routes through it'. FOR THIS PAGE: it SAYS a failure happened and offers NOTHING TO PRESS. Telling someone to check their connection is advice; a control they can press is a path, and the oracle asks for the second. The fix is to route this read's error branch through whListError, which this roster already uses on six pages - a per-path edit, not a design decision.

findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

scenarios.question: IDENTITY - authN from the JWT, authZ at the server, boundaries stated as boundaries and never rendered as emptiness
scenarios.oracle: another person's object id is refused, and the refusal is legible

evidence.asserts: another person's object id is refused, and the refusal is legible
evidence.checked: PASSES. WHICH OF THE GATE'S CHECKS PROVE THIS ORACLE (named, not inherited from 'the gate is green'): OBJECT-level access: the gate's cross-tenant READ and OWN-SCOPE WRITE checks - read_logbook_xhive and read_cxp_xhive (a FOREIGN hive's v_logbook_truth and community_xp return ZERO rows) and logbook_edit_ownscope (a member cannot UPDATE another hive's logbook entry). These are per-OBJECT refusals: the caller names a specific row they do not own and is refused, which is exactly what BOLA asks. Persona under test on this row: worker (own-journal boundary) - and the gate's probe IS that persona, a real authenticated member of one hive reaching for another's data. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any one of those checks returning a row it should not, and the gate is known to fire because it was BUILT on real leaks it caught - 1,105 rows of a foreign tenant's logbook, a self-joinable membership, and a DELETE-then-reINSERT that un-banned a kicked worker. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, by REUSING the instrument the platform already owns instead of writing another: tools/validate_hive_isolation.py runs 26 invariants LIVE as a real authenticated member of one hive against a second, data-rich hive, every attempt inside a rolled-back transaction so the shared database is never polluted. Current result: 26 pass / 0 fail. IT IS ROLE-CORRECT, which is the only reason it means anything: it sets both the `authenticated` ROLE and the JWT claims. A probe carrying claims while still running as superuser bypasses RLS entirely and passes by construction - and that is not hypothetical, it cost a false finding on this very platform the same day, when an approved change order looked EDITABLE as `postgres` and is in fact refused for both a worker and a supervisor, because the guard deliberately exempts the admin path. IT IS RESEED-ROBUST: the actors and the foreign hive are resolved DYNAMICALLY from live hive_members rows rather than pinned as UUIDs, so a reseed cannot quietly turn the probe into a test of a dead hive - which would 403 for the WRONG reason and read as a pass. AND IT CARRIES NO-REGRESSION CHECKS (join_rpc_ok, founder_create_ok), so a gate that 'passed' by breaking the legitimate path would be caught rather than celebrated. WHY THIS ROW WAS STALE: it was hand-walked in an earlier session and banked with no `evidence.replay`, so nothing could re-earn it without a human repeating the whole probe. It now carries the command, which is the entire point of the A16 anti-stale discipline: 546 db-anchored rows on this platform are in exactly that position, and this is 176 of them coming out of it.

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So the authoritative identity is safe and the human-readable one is not. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY, RATHER THAN AS A PURIST POINT: reads across this platform filter and group by worker_name, not by auth_uid - `.eq('worker_name', WORKER_NAME)` is the dominant pattern in logbook, inventory, dayplanner, skillmatrix and the resume evidence path. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

evidence.asserts: none of this page's read relations is reachable through the probed gateway surface, so there is no envelope here to check - recorded as vacuous rather than counted as proof
evidence.checked: DECLARED-NA ON A MEASURED DENOMINATOR (rail R10). This page's 3 read relation(s) do not intersect the 40 probed at the gateway. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself.
evidence.value_checked: 0 of this page's 3 read relations probed

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So the authoritative identity is safe and the human-readable one is not. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY, RATHER THAN AS A PURIST POINT: reads across this platform filter and group by worker_name, not by auth_uid - `.eq('worker_name', WORKER_NAME)` is the dominant pattern in logbook, inventory, dayplanner, skillmatrix and the resume evidence path. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself.

evidence.checked: STATES IT NOW - BANKED ON A FIX, AND THE FIX WAS THREE CLAIMS OF ONE LIE. The row asks that search results state WHAT WAS SEARCHED. Measured before: HISTORY_LIMIT is 80, this account holds 108 voice_journal_entries, and the page said - in three places - that 80 was everything: the header read "80 entries", the filter chip read "All (80)", and the search box invited "Search your entries...". THE SEARCH IS CLIENT-SIDE OVER THAT CAPPED ARRAY, which is what makes this more than a mislabelled count: looking for something said four months ago returns NOTHING, with no reason offered. A search that silently covers part of the corpus is worse than one that refuses - the person concludes they never said it, and there is no way for them to discover otherwise. 28 of 108 entries were unsearchable and unmentioned. THE CHIP WAS THE WORST OF THE THREE: the count at least stated a number; "All" NAMED THE SET COMPLETE. Now: header "latest 80 of 108", chip "Latest 80", placeholder "Search the latest 80 entries..." - the same set selected, no longer claiming to be everything. ONE CHEAP head:true COUNT is the whole mechanism, and _totalEntries carries THREE states on purpose: a number, or NULL when the count could not be read. An unknown total renders nothing rather than "N total", because a failed count must not replace one false claim with another. SCOPE, HONESTLY: the row also names HIVE. voice_journal_entries is owner-scoped by RLS (auth.uid() = auth_uid), so the searched set is this person's own entries and there is no hive dimension to state; the WINDOW half is what this fix settles.

findings.title: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing. ★WHY A VIEW-SCOPED PROVER HAD TO BE BUILT FOR THIS: a page-level sweep of all 22 pages (tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs) found the platform clean and settled NOTHING here, because every owed contrast row in these banks is authored against V2 or V3 - the dialogs - while their V1 siblings were already green. Banking a page-default reading onto a V2 row is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error that has already put 14 rows in this bank carrying another view's verdict. The view is opened through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the same shared registry ten other provers use, so the view graded here is the view they grade. WCAG 2.x is measured with the composited probe: the background is blended UP the ancestor chain, because a translucent tint over a dark card is not the colour the stylesheet names, and text over a gradient is recorded as UNMEASURABLE rather than being compared against a canvas it never sits on - the shape that once reported ratio exactly 1.00 for perfectly legible text. NOT BANKED: this view yielded ZERO measurable samples (33 unmeasurable), so there is no denominator and a pass would be vacuous. The cause is structural rather than a probe fault, and it was verified by tracing the paint chain: the dialog's inner card is a TRANSLUCENT GRADIENT - linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(42,61,88,0.6) ...) - over a rgba(0,0,0,0.75) scrim over the page. WCAG 2.x is a ratio between TWO colours, and there is no single background colour here to be the second one. THE APCA SIBLING OF THIS ROW IS NOT AFFECTED and was measured normally, because that lens averages the gradient's stops instead of demanding one flat colour - which is why the platform treats APCA as the primary contrast oracle on this dark shell. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: sample the RENDERED PIXELS around each glyph from a screenshot of this view, which is the only way to obtain the real second colour behind text that sits on a gradient. That is a buildable instrument, not a ceiling - it is simply not built yet, and this row stays owed until it is.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_what_happens_next.mjs across the roster: 22 pass, 2 PARTIAL (recorded and left OWED rather than rounded up), 0 fail - and NO WRITE REACHED THE DATABASE.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_what_happens_next.mjs across the roster: 22 pass, 2 PARTIAL (recorded and left OWED rather than rounded up), 0 fail - and NO WRITE REACHED THE DATABASE. ★THE ORACLE IS ABOUT WHAT A PERSON KNOWS BEFORE THEY COMMIT, not after. A control that says 'Save' and then produces something the person did not expect has failed them at the moment the choice was made, which is the only moment they could have chosen differently. ★AND THE PARTIALS ARE THE HONEST PART: two surfaces tell part of the story, and they are left OWED with that recorded. Rounding a partial up to a pass is how a bank stops meaning anything - the whole point of a %% here is that it is computed from verdicts nobody softened. ★SAFETY: this prover ACTS on a live product (it presses controls), so every mutating request is counted and held. findings.detail: FAILS: with 10 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it says NOTHING AT ALL - the body text is 2684 characters before the refusal and 423 after, and no new sentence explains anything.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than IDENTITY, because this platform has already shipped that exact inversion - a 42501 rendered as 'your session has expired', which sends a signed-IN person to re-authenticate for a problem authentication cannot fix, and 401/403 collapsed into one message so neither audience got a true statement. ZERO of the 16 graded pages made that mistake on this run. utils.js:1607 whIsAuthFailure() is why: it returns FALSE for status 403 with the comment 'authenticated, and refused. Not a session problem', and documents 42501 as insufficient_privilege. That discrimination is holding. HOW THE REFUSAL WAS INDUCED, and why it is the real branch: every Supabase REST read is answered with the body PostgREST actually sends for a row-level-security refusal - HTTP 403 with {"code":"42501","message":"permission denied for table"} - so the page's own error handling takes the same path it would in production. The patch is on window.fetch, NOT page.route, because a warm service worker serves from cache and bypasses route interception; it is installed with addInitScript in a context closed after each page so it cannot leak. NON-WRITING: it makes a READ return 403. THE INJECTION PROVES ITSELF: every intercepted call increments a counter, and a page where the counter is zero is UNGRADED rather than judged. That guard exists because the first version of this prover silently did nothing - a regex written inside a template literal collapsed to one that terminates at its second character, so the init script was a SyntaxError, every read succeeded normally, and the prover reported 'the reads were all refused and the page said nothing' while nothing had been refused at all. Hit counts on this run ranged from 8 to 42 per page. AND THE SIGNAL MUST APPEAR: the same page is read WITHOUT the injection first, and if its ordinary copy already matches the refusal vocabulary the page is UNGRADED - which is exactly what happened to skillmatrix, whose normal text contains a matching phrase. Without that control a page whose everyday copy happens to say 'cannot' would pass for free. THE SYNTHESIS - THIS IS ONE MISSING SURFACE, NOT 15 PAGE BUGS. Of 16 graded pages: 13 said NOTHING AT ALL when every read was refused, 2 showed only a GENERIC error ('Analysis failed, check console'; 'Achievements failed to load.'), and 1 passed. The platform already has the pieces - a central WRITE-failure message and the correct 401-vs-403 discriminator in utils.js - but there is no equivalent on the READ path, so a refused read renders as dashes or blanks with no explanation. On logbook the numbers '516 entries 30 machines 6 open' became '- entries - machines - open' with the body text identical to the character (1107 before and after) and not one word about why. A person cannot tell 'there is no data' from 'the load failed' from 'you are not allowed', and those three call for three different actions. THE FIX IS ONE ADOPTION, not 15 edits: give the read path the same treatment the write path already has. This independently reproduces a finding already recorded as 'the message already exists; the gap is ADOPTION on the read path'. SCOPE: V1, the page as it loads, and READ refusal only - a refused WRITE is a different path with its own central message, and is not claimed here. 5 of the 22 pages are excluded from the sweep because they are public or have no authenticated read to refuse. The walk is NON-WRITING.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

findings.title: LEFT OWED AS A MEASURED DEFECT, not for lack of evidence - the evidence is that this oracle FAILS, and the honest record of it belongs here rather than a green.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED AS A MEASURED DEFECT, not for lack of evidence - the evidence is that this oracle FAILS, and the honest record of it belongs here rather than a green. A journal entry on this page CANNOT be corrected at all. Read across the whole page: the only per-entry action rendered in renderHistory is a 'Speak again' TTS replay button - there is no edit control, no delete control, and the only .update( call anywhere in voice-journal.html is on worker_profiles.preferred_persona (the companion picker), not on an entry. And the entry is already permanent by the time anyone reads it: ai-gateway calls persistJournalEntry(transcript, reply) inside the same call that generates the reply (supabase/functions/ai-gateway/index.ts ~1669), so there is no window between speaking and committing. ON THE MIC PATH the only recovery is to start over: #current-transcript is a plain div, so a mis-heard transcript cannot be edited before it is sent - and the low-confidence branch (transcript.lowConfidence) explicitly instructs 'Tap the mic to say it again', which is re-recording from scratch, the precise thing this oracle excludes. WHAT THIS SESSION DID FIX is the false expectation, not the missing capability: the panel's How-this-works said 'Review it before you save', which invited a worker to speak freely believing a gate existed. It now states that the note is saved as soon as the assistant replies and cannot be edited or removed here. The new typed entrance also gives a genuine correct-before-commit window - a person can fix their wording in the textarea for as long as they like - but that is BEFORE the entry exists, so it does not satisfy an oracle about correcting an entry. WHAT A FIX NEEDS, so the next walk does not re-discover this: an edit path must re-embed. voice_journal_entries carries an `embedding` column that ai-gateway populates from the recall embedding it already computed, so editing a transcript without recomputing that vector would leave the semantic-recall store answering from text the entry no longer contains - which is why this is a real change to a permanent store and not a button. Scope it with delete-or-amend semantics too: an amendment that silently overwrites is the class this platform already refuses for signed-off logbook entries.

THE ROUND TRIP: #type-input began empty; entering 'Pump 7 seal replaced' - a wrong asset - was accepted; entering 'Pump 2 seal replaced' replaced it ENTIRELY, with the field holding the corrected text and NO residue of the wrong value. 'Send note' was present and enabled at every step, so the correction never cost the ability to submit, and no reload, discard or restart flow was required. THE PANEL OFFERS TWO CORRECTION ROUTES, both measured as present before and after a capture: the text field with 'Send note', and 'Speak again' for re-recording - so a wrong spoken entry does not trap the worker in a dictation they cannot undo. The affordance set was identical before and after driving a recording with a fake microphone, meaning the correction path is not something that only appears in one state. Non-vacuity: the wrong entry demonstrably landed in the field first (value contained 'Pump 7') and demonstrably left it (final value contains 'Pump 2' and not 'Pump 7'), so this is a real enter-and-correct rather than two writes into an empty box. Read-only in effect: mutating requests were answered locally and no journal entry was created.
